Just how free is Windows 10 going to be, and for how long?

Microsoft is releasing arguably the most important version of Windows in its history this month and we don’t know how long it will be supported or what future costs we will be charged after this unknown period.

And this is different from every other release of Windows how? Oh that's right, you get it for free up front...

What's there to complain about in that?

Look I am a huge opensource proponent, and I regularly use Linux at home and at work, but I can't be spun up into a fervor over this. I hate it when people spread FUD just because they don't yet know all the details.

So... Basically they provide free support for 2-4 years on a free operating system and then the customer has had 2-4 years to decide whether they want to buy it for more support?

I fail to see the bad in this.
Agreed. Some people will try to find a reason to whine about everything.

Sites really have a hard time understanding 'free for the lifetime of your device', don't they?

It's not that hard, come on.

It's free to those that upgrade for the first year, and barring any major revisions, it'll be free to those people for the rest of their and their device's lives.

If you don't saddle yourself with an OEM license, you can use your key on your next machine, too.

I don't understand why people are trying to make a mountain out of this. If we go back to Windows 8 - MS were praised for selling it cheaply and sticking to the old service pack model.

Offer it for free? "Let's get annoyed!"

Another of those *nix fans here: To me, it sound obvious that when you operate a software, and you have a problem, you pay for the service needed to make it work (How many of you maintain your own car, rebuilt your own roof?).

From this paradigm, we have to add that most people don't "suffer" from buying Windows, since it is massively coming pre-bundled. Few realize a $500 laptop is $300 without it, essentially because it is very hard to find that same laptop on the open market (Hint: Asus, Amazon, Italy or Germany).

Back to the point: People don't know.

There comes the strangeness: The customer doesn't know he paid for something that comes as natural to him, and now hears that it will come free first, then as a subscription later : I believe M$ is testing the waters here, and may, or may not, monetize W10 directly later.

If adoption is instant, and then people protest over the Subscription Scheme, M$ can drop it, and follow the Mobile Economy way of an App Store to harvest some $$$ from third-party apps and services, or end up with a complete turn around, and adopt the FOSS Sustainability usage of not paying for the product, but for training, special applications, massive deployments and such.

At the peak of piracy around M$ products, that would have been a very logical path. Now that we are at some sort of peak around the "I don't need a PC anymore, I can do stuff on anything from anywhere" maybe someone over at Redmond had the penny droppin', and is leading them in a promising way. For them and their future, I mean: a truly free W10 on every machine that is not a Tablet or a Phone or a TV-attached device of some sorts? Sounds just about right, sounds just about the way it works in 2015 (Or they would have to have it as Apple does it, and the whole Nokia experience isn't that encouraging right now).

Can you give some examples of KOTOR mods? I've been considering picking it up off of Steam and hadn't even considered the possibility of mods.

Mods can range from cosmetic, as in adding armors or clothes, to gameplay related, as in changing level progression and making it easier/harder to progress.
